How predictable is it?

Measured over-to-over variation averages 3.10 runs, which makes this a volatile ground - over-to-over scoring swings widely, so a required rate here is less reliable than the same rate elsewhere. The death overs are the loosest part at 4.49.

Reading a chase here

A required rate means different things at different grounds. At Warner Park, St Kitts the powerplay goes at 6.99 an over batting first, so a chase that is level with the rate after four overs is genuinely level — not ahead, and not behind. The phase table above is what the model uses to judge that, rather than a single national average.

Where these numbers come from

Ball-by-ball records for every T20 played at this ground in the dataset, aggregated per phase and per innings. The same records feed the live win probability on this site, which scores 81.5% across 19,340 predictions on 2,546 matches it had never seen during training — the method and calibration table are on the accuracy page.

No ball-tracking is used: speed, swing and spin measurements are not available at this scale, and these figures are delivery outcomes only.
